title: Book One · Chapter 144: River Street Day
story:
The school says yes on a bright morning. Miss Wu brings the news after the reading lesson. They may use a room for Our River Street. It will be a Saturday, three weeks after Ronan's birthday. Visitors may come at two in the afternoon. The room will close at four.

Leo holds both hands above his head. “Can we move the tables on Friday?” Mei asks. She means the Friday before the display. Ronan is very happy. For a moment, he forgets his first question.

Miss Wu writes the time on the board. Under it she writes three things. Adults must help set up. Everyone must help put the room back. Nothing may be sold.

“It is a day for showing,” she says. “A small River Street Day.”

The children repeat the name. It is easy to say. Leo puts a little door under the words. Mei looks at him, then at his drawing. He has drawn the same square door again. He adds a roof before she can speak.

Ronan copies the time exactly. He keeps the paper flat on the way home. He wants everyone to read the time clearly. Mr Qiu reads it first. He says he may close the table for part of that afternoon, but he needs to think about customers.

“You can come for a short time,” Ronan says.

“That may work.”

Mrs Lan says she will decide nearer the day. She has another visit to arrange. Ronan puts a small question mark beside her name. Other people have already said yes. He can go on with the plan. Mrs Lan can decide about her visit later.

Mum reads the no-selling line. She lays her hand on the blue bag.

“Then one bag is enough. I will not spend three weeks making a shop they have not asked for.”

“Will you come?”

“I plan to. We need to look at my work times.”

They finish supper. Then Dad comes home. Ronan has saved a warm bowl for him. He puts the date beside it. Dad washes his hands, sits down, and reads.

“A Saturday.”

“From two until four.”

“I work Saturdays.”

Ronan knows that. Dad worked on Saturdays long before this display plan. But he wants Dad to be there. Now Dad may not be able to come. Ronan looks down at the date.

“You could ask Mr Sun.”

“I can ask about the hours. I cannot tell you yes tonight.”

“You have three weeks.”

Dad looks at him. “I can ask him during those three weeks. But will he agree? I do not know yet.”

Mum gives Dad his tea. Ronan moves the invitation away from the bowl before a drop can reach it. Then he sits beside him and tells him about the room. He describes the clear route, the quiet game, and the chair for older visitors.

Dad listens while he eats. He asks one question about the table legs. Ronan does not know the answer. He writes it on the back of the paper.

Ronan begins a calendar on a clean page. He marks his birthday first and the school Saturday three weeks later. The spaces between them look empty. He puts the room check in one and the picture work in another. He leaves several spaces clear. He will still have schoolwork each day. He must leave time for meals and play too.

Outside, Mr Qiu closes the grey table. He is still using the place Mrs Lan agreed to. Inside, Mum puts her name card in the blue bag. It can stay safe there. Ronan has a date and a room. Each person can choose a picture, object, or story for it. Ronan puts his calendar away. Tomorrow he can ask about the table legs. Dad needs time to ask about work too.

---

重点表达：set up＝布置；nearer the day＝临近当天；plan to＝计划做。

情节提示：calendar＝日历；route＝行走路线；invitation＝邀请卡。

理解：1. 河街日将在什么时间、什么地点举行？2. Dad 为什么没有答应一定参加？
